title: THE FIRE THAT REFUSED TO CONSUME
paragraphs:
THE FIRE THAT REFUSED TO CONSUME
What Science Cannot Explain… God Uses to Reveal Himself
There are moments in life where everything inside you feels like it’s burning… but somehow you’re still here.

Not destroyed.
Not finished.
Just… burning.
And if you’ve ever wondered why you didn’t break the way you thought you would… this is where your story meets a bush that should have turned to ash—but didn’t.
Somewhere in the wilderness of Midian, a fugitive shepherd named Moses was walking through the ordinary dust of an ordinary day when eternity interrupted him.
The ancient Hebrew text doesn’t rush the moment. It lingers.

וַיֵּרָא מַלְאַךְ יְהוָה אֵלָיו בְּלַבַּת־אֵשׁ מִתּוֹךְ הַסְּנֶה
Vayera mal’akh YHWH elav belabbat-esh mitokh has-seneh
“And the Angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush…” (Exodus 3:2)
But then something impossible happens.

וְהַסְּנֶה אֵינֶנּוּ אֻכָּל
Vehas-seneh einennu ukal
“…yet the bush was not consumed.”
Let that sit on your soul for a second.
Fire… without destruction.
Science would call this a contradiction.
Fire, by definition, oxidises material. It consumes fuel. It breaks molecular bonds. Heat transfers energy until structure collapses. In every natural model, fire destroys what it touches.
Unless…
The energy source is not dependent on the material.
Unless the fire is not drawing from the bush—but sustaining it.
Unless what Moses saw wasn’t natural fire at all… but divine presence expressed in a way his human mind could barely comprehend.

Even modern theories—like plasma phenomena, cold flames, or self-sustaining chemical reactions—fall short. They can mimic aspects of the event, but none explain a flame that burns indefinitely without degrading its host.
Because this wasn’t chemistry.
This was revelation.

God didn’t choose a mountain.
He didn’t choose a palace.
He didn’t choose a temple.
He chose a bush.
Insignificant. Overlooked. Common.
Just like Moses felt.
Just like you might feel.
And maybe that’s the part no one told you… the miracle isn’t just that the bush didn’t burn.
It’s that God chose something so ordinary to reveal something so holy.
Because what you’ve been calling “just your life”… might be the exact place God wants to reveal His glory.
The Greek translation in the Septuagint intensifies the moment:

καὶ ὁ βάτος καίετο πυρί, καὶ ὁ βάτος οὐ κατεκαίετο
kai ho batos kaieto pyri, kai ho batos ou katekaieto
“The bush burned with fire, yet the bush was not consumed.”
Not “was burning” temporarily.
It “kept burning.”
Continuous. Sustained. Supernatural.
And suddenly… it becomes less about the bush and more about the One in the fire.
Because later, the voice speaks.

אֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה
Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh
“I AM WHO I AM.” (Exodus 3:14)

Not “I was.”
Not “I will be.”
I AM.
Present. Active. Unchanging.
And here’s where it gets personal.
What if the fire you’ve been trying to escape… is actually where God is trying to meet you?
What if the pressure didn’t come to destroy you… but to reveal Him through you?
You thought you were falling apart.
But you’re still here.
You thought it would consume you.
But it didn’t.
Because when God is the source… the fire refines, not ruins.
That’s the science no lab can measure.
Grace that sustains what should have collapsed.
Presence that holds together what should have shattered.
And if you’ve ever lived through something that should have broken you completely… then you already know this truth in your bones.
You’ve been a burning bush.
Still standing.
Still breathing.
Still somehow… not consumed.
This is the scandal.
That God doesn’t wait for you to become something impressive.
He steps into your mess, your past, your regret, your wilderness… and lights it with His presence.
And suddenly, what looked like destruction becomes divine encounter.
Moses walked away from that moment different.
Not because the bush changed…
But because he realised God had been there all along.
And maybe that’s why this is hitting you right now.
Because deep down, you know… something in your life is burning.
And you don’t understand why it hasn’t destroyed you yet.
This is your answer.
God is closer than you think.
Moses didn’t just observe the fire.
He turned aside.
He leaned in.
He responded.
“Let me turn aside and see this great sight…” (Exodus 3:3)
And everything changed from that moment.
So be honest.
Have you been ignoring the fire?
Avoiding the conviction?
Silencing that quiet voice calling you deeper?
Don’t stay silent on something this personal.
Someone else reading your words might realise they’re not alone.

And if you feel called to go deeper—to actually grow, to understand Scripture beyond surface-level, to strengthen your faith in a world that constantly pulls you away—then step into something more intentional.
Because this isn’t just content… this is discipleship.
Not because faith is for sale…
But because commitment changes how deeply you receive.
If this spoke to you, don’t just feel it.
Respond to it.
Because the same God who burned in that bush… is still speaking today.
And He’s not trying to destroy you.
He’s trying to reveal Himself through you.
You were never meant to be consumed… only transformed.
